exposure: natural mating versus in vitro fertilization (IVF)
mouse strain (C57BL/6J, BALB/c, NSG, KM) as GF foster mothers
cohort: The study involved donor mice, germ-free mice produced through cesarean derivation, and four strains of mice (C57BL/6J, BALB/c, NSG, KM) used as germ-free foster mothers.
finding: Optimizing surgical methods, specifically preserving the female reproductive tract during cesarean section (FRT-CS), significantly improved fetal survival rates and sterility, while IVF enhanced experimental reproducibility, and BALB/c and NSG mice demonstrated superior nursing and weaning success as germ-free foster mothers.
mod_finding: Optimizing surgical methods that preserve the female reproductive tract during cesarean section (FRT-CS) significantly improved fetal survival rates while maintaining sterility compared to other cesarean section methods.
